chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: His Baptist church and Geneva Hurris, later met in New Orleans
summary: He names the church on Independence and Charlotte and the preacher's daughter who played piano, whom he met again at the Dew Drop Inn.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Speaking of church, you talked about singin' in church. What church was it you went to there in Kansas City?

I went to the Baptist Church, Reverend Hurris's (?) church. It was on Independence Avenue and Charlotte, right down the street from my house. That's where we had a...his daughter played the piano. Later on, I met her in New Orleans. She was playin' and workin' in a nightclub.
So she went on and played professionally.

Yeah, she was good. She was playin' piano when she's a kid. I hadn't seen her in years and went to New Orleans, Louisiana, and met her...run up on her. She's in a bar...a place called the Dew Drop Inn.
When was that? How long ago was that?
Oh, that's been about fifteen...twenty years ago.
